newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 16.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Calenergy launched the first stage of a hostile bid for New York State Electric & Gas.
* Chase Manhattan and Citicorp reported second quarter earning sin line with expectations.
* Reynolds Metals is contemplating shedding all or part of its $1 billion U.S. aluminum can business.
* Retail sales rebounded modestly in June.
* The Veterans Affairs department has begun processing the first in a potential tidal wave of compensation claims for smoking-related diseases and deaths.
* An effort to curb global warming could result in a substantial increase in energy prices.
* The British Telecom contract to buy MCI Communications contains an exemption that would seem to neutralize concerns that BT might seek to renegotiate its deal.
* Intel net jumped 58 percent in the quarter.
* Texas Instruments second quarter operating profit soared to $224 million from $41 million.
* Boeing's latest talks with the EC its merger with McDonnell failed to produce a compromise, with the commission moving a step closer to blocking the deal.
* Savannah Foods plans to merge with one of its large sugar suppliers, Florida Crystals.
* Stocks rose, lifted by the technology sector.
* Merrill Lynch, Smith Barney and PaineWebber posted quarterly profit gains.
* Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer reported strong gains in quarterly earnings.
* Brazilian stocks were pounded for a third session.
* Travelers Group posted a 15 percent gain in second quarter earnings.
* Kia Motors and 17 affiliated received special protection from their creditors.

* Japan's financial reforms got their most powerful acknowledgment yet Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan and Swiss Bank agreed to form a string of new joint ventures and take three percent stakes in each other.
* Tokyo stocks fell to profit taking.
* Treasury securities were flat to slightly higher after Tuesday's release of retail sales data for June.
* Shares in Internet-releated stocks are zooming while those in companies that make in-line skates, bicycles, athletic footware and snowboarding equipment are weak.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
